sources.title: One Head is Better than Two: A Polynomial Restriction for Propositional Definite Horn Forgetting
sources.venue: Journal of Logic, Language and Information 34, 2025
sources.role: Primary recent single-head polynomial-forgetting comparison and warning that unrestricted definite-Horn forgetting may be exponentially larger.

new_repository_result: The JANUS route has an executable proof-carrying Horn projector, a uniform polynomial theorem for single-head messages under guarded joins, complete explicit Horn merge/separator extraction, and a family-specific exact 2^n lower bound for unrestricted boundary-only Horn CNF projection.
decisive_redirect: The missing Horn operation is not explicit-message equivalence; it is polynomial-size projection and join closure. The surviving route requires a richer Horn message language or charged isolation of head-disjoint single-head regions.
lineage_note: Stacked on PR #52 / C039.1 pure-affine factors. Canonical cycle is C039.2; c039-1 paths are replay aliases.
claim_boundary: No source or C039.2 artifact rules out richer Horn circuits, existential Horn modules, portfolio-guided decompositions, or resolves P versus NP.
